title: Growing buckwheat shoots
subtitle: Mild, nutty cotyledons from unhulled buckwheat seed, cut in 8 to 12 days
excerpt: Buckwheat shoots produce large triangular cotyledons with a mild, slightly nutty flavour. The cycle is 8 to 12 days, one of the faster non-brassica crops. The seed must be unhulled (the triangular dark-hulled grain); hulled buckwheat groats will not germinate.
sourceNotes: UMass Extension microgreens guides (open-access). Cornell Cooperative Extension indoor growing material. Standard microgreen-growing practice synthesised from extension service material.

glossaryTerms.definition: Watering by setting the growing tray inside a second tray filled with water, allowing the growing medium to draw moisture up from below. Keeps the seedling surface dry and reduces mould and damping-off risk in microgreen trays.

A fungal condition where seedling stems collapse and rot at the soil surface. Caused by Pythium, Fusarium, and Rhizoctonia species in warm, wet, poorly-ventilated conditions. Common in overcrowded or overwatered microgreen trays.

content.text: Buckwheat shoots are a year-round indoor tray crop with an 8 to 12 day cycle. Sow unhulled buckwheat seed on a pre-dampened seed compost tray, blackout for three to four days, then grow in light until the large triangular cotyledons are 5 to 8 cm tall. The flavour is mild and slightly nutty with a faint earthiness. Buckwheat is not a grass; it is a broadleaf plant, and the cotyledons are larger and more substantial than grass microgreens.

The key requirement for buckwheat microgreens is that the seed must be unhulled: the intact dark-green or dark-brown triangular grain with the outer hull in place. Hulled buckwheat (the cream or pale grey groats sold as a grain food) has had the hull removed and will not germinate.

Light: a bright south-facing windowsill in spring and summer. A grow light 15 to 20 cm above the tray at 14 to 16 hours per day is recommended in winter. Buckwheat cotyledons in low light become tall and leggy, with weaker stem structure and reduced flavour.
Temperature: 18 to 24°C. Buckwheat germinates best in warmth; below 15°C germination becomes slow and unreliable. It is not a cold-tolerant microgreen crop.

Day 0: sow. Fill the tray with pre-dampened seed compost to within 1 cm of the rim. Scatter unhulled buckwheat seed at 100 to 150 g per 25 cm tray; buckwheat is large and heavy, and needs a dense sowing to fill the tray. Spread the seeds in a single layer. Do not cover with soil. Press gently into contact with the medium.
Days 1 to 4: blackout. Cover with a second tray, weighted with 500 g to 1 kg. The weight aids hull separation as the shoot pushes through it. Remove when the majority of shoots are 3 to 5 cm tall.
Day 5 onward: light. The large triangular cotyledons open and turn deep green within 24 to 48 hours.
daily: set the growing tray inside a second tray with 1 to 2 cm of water. Buckwheat shoots have substantial root systems and use more water than small brassica microgreens; check daily.

Days 8 to 12: cut. When cotyledons are fully open and 5 to 8 cm tall, cut 1 cm above the medium surface. Some hulls will remain attached to the cotyledons; this is normal. Rinse under cold water and pick off any remaining hulls before serving. Use fresh or refrigerate for up to two days.

attrs.heading: Troubleshooting
attrs.intro: Common problems on buckwheat shoot trays.

items.symptom: Seeds fail to germinate at all
items.cause: Hulled buckwheat groats sown instead of unhulled grain.
items.fix: Check the seed: unhulled buckwheat has a dark outer hull and an angular triangular shape. Hulled groats are pale cream or grey and will not germinate. Buy from a microgreen seed supplier specifying unhulled seed.

items.symptom: Seed hulls clinging to cotyledons after the blackout phase
items.cause: The buckwheat hull does not always release cleanly.
items.fix: Mist the hulls with water and wait 20 minutes; they soften and can be removed by hand. A heavier blackout weight on the next batch helps hulls detach during germination.
Warm the room above 18°C. Ensure the seed compost is thoroughly pre-dampened before sowing; buckwheat needs reliable moisture to germinate evenly.

items.symptom: Mould on medium surface between seeds
items.cause: The dense sowing holds moisture between seeds in warm conditions.
items.fix: Bottom-water only; avoid surface wetting. Ensure airflow around the tray. Rinse soaked seeds before sowing to remove surface sugars.

content.text: The seed for buckwheat microgreens must be unhulled buckwheat: the whole grain with the dark angular hull intact. Microgreen seed suppliers label it clearly; health food stores often stock unhulled buckwheat for sprouting. Do not confuse with buckwheat groats (the hulled grain used in porridge), which will not germinate.
risk is moderate given the dense sowing and the warm conditions buckwheat prefers. Bottom-water only and maintain airflow.
